envHint: These values look like secrets, so they are kept out of the Compose file. Save this as a .env file next to it (and keep it private).
warning.convert.unsupported_flag: The option {{detail}} is not converted. Check whether you need it.
warning.convert.rm: --rm (remove at exit) has no Compose equivalent: the container stays after it stops.
warning.convert.foreground: There was no -d: docker run would stay attached. In Compose, use `docker compose up -d` to run it in the background.
fromContainers.explain: Pick containers that are already running and get the Compose file that recreates them. Their settings, including environment variables, are read once and nothing is changed or saved. Secret-looking values go to a separate .env.
warning.convert.already_compose: This container already belongs to the Compose project “{{detail}}”: converting it creates a second copy of its description.
warning.convert.privileged: {{detail}} runs privileged: it can do almost anything on the machine. Check that you want to keep it.
warning.convert.docker_socket: {{detail}} can control Docker itself (it mounts the Docker socket).
warning.convert.env_inline: Some variables of {{detail}} stay readable in the file because they do not look like secrets. Check them before sharing it.
warning.convert.truncated: {{detail}} had values or lists too long to be read whole: the file is incomplete.
warning.convert.host_access: {{detail}} shares the machine's network or processes, or holds SYS_ADMIN: it is hardly isolated.
warning.convert.secret_inline: A variable of {{detail}} looks like a secret but its name is unusual: it stays readable in the file. Move it to .env by hand.
